title: Synthesis and Tribological Characteristics of High-Performance Self-Lubricating CoCrFeNiMo<sub>x</sub>-Ni/MoS<sub>2</sub>-Ag-Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> Composites.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: CoCrFeNiMo high-entropy alloy powders, Ni, MoS2, Ag, Cr2O3
recollection.intervention: Guess: Powder metallurgy or sintering to create composite materials with embedded lubricants and hard phases
recollection.structure: Guess: Composite structure with dispersed MoS2 (solid lubricant), Ag (soft metal), and Cr2O3 (hard phase) within a CoCrFeNiMo matrix
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Self-lubricating effect from MoS2 and Ag reduces friction, while Cr2O3 improves wear resistance; synergy between phases enhances tribological properties
recollection.results: Guess: Lower friction coefficient and wear rate compared to base alloy; quantitative results likely include friction coefficient values (e.g., <0.2) and wear rate reductions (e.g., 50% improvement)

score.note: The recollection gives only generic powder-metallurgy synthesis and title-derived constituent roles. It misses the key intervention of varying Mo content (x = 0.2, 0.5, 1), the Mo-induced lattice distortion and σ phase, and the temperature-dependent transition from MoS2/Ag lubrication to oxide/silver-molybdate glaze formation. Its suggested friction coefficient (<0.2) and 50% wear improvement are unsupported and do not match the reported minimum coefficient of 0.23 or the measured wear rates.
